elements.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer shall pay Vendor no liquidated damages"
"and no penalty, and no amount in the nature of either"

elements.element: Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: Redline addresses only invoice-late liquidated damages; no early-termination fee cap appears in 7.7.

elements.element: That fee is the sole liquidated amount under the Agreement
elements.evidence: No sole-liquidated-amount language in the revised 7.7.

offending_extra_words: and no amount in the nature of either
reasons: Preferred level is complete: the operative words now provide that Customer pays no liquidated damages and no penalty for late invoices, deleting the fifteen percent weekly charge.

The added catch-all "and no amount in the nature of either" duplicates the protection already given by "no liquidated damages and no penalty" and is more than needed to reach the preferred position; deleting the payment obligation (or flipping the two operative nouns) suffices.

The retained trailing words "for each week the invoice remains unpaid" leave a slightly awkward residue attached to a nil obligation, but they create no contradiction and Vendor's other non-payment remedies elsewhere remain effective.
Fallback is separate and unmet, which is irrelevant because the locked target is preferred.
